$comment: Every invalid fixture, and what the schema has to refuse it for. A negative fixture without a declared refusal is a file that could start passing for a reason nobody intended, so the suite asserts both directions: every fixture here is refused at the path named, and every fixture on disk is named here.

c0-that-executed-the-target-behaviour.reason: C0 is evidence obtained without executing the target behaviour. A record that executed it is not static evidence.

c1-forced-by-a-synthetic-workload.reason: Synthetic input does not make a record C1. C1 requires a claim-material substitution, and this record names none.

c2-naming-no-component-that-executed.reason: A record that executed the target behaviour names at least one component that ran. Otherwise the level asserts an execution the record cannot describe.

c2-with-a-claim-material-substitution.reason: Real is relative to the claim. A claim-material substitution puts the record at C1 however much of the rest of the path was real.

c3-with-criteria-declared-after-the-run.reason: C3 requires criteria registered before the run. A criterion written afterwards cannot fail.

c3-without-declared-representativeness.reason: C3 requires declared representativeness with its assumptions written down. Without it the record is a C2 run under an undeclared workload.

c4-from-a-public-cloud-experiment.reason: C4 requires an organization, a workload that depended on the system, and a stated observation period. A cloud experiment is C2, or C3 where it meets the representativeness requirements.

c4-without-documented-known-gaps.reason: C4 requires documented conditions and known gaps. A production window with nothing said about what it did not cover reads as covering everything.

legacy-record-enriched-with-a-level.reason: An unmigrated record carries no evidence level. Copying the superseded certificationLevel into evidenceLevel is the reclassification V1-S5-012-PR2 exists to do properly.

legacy-record-without-its-carried-classi.reason: An unmigrated record keeps its v1alpha1 classification verbatim. Dropping it destroys the audit trail the migration is reviewed against.

migrated-record-citing-no-evidence.reason: A migrated record cites at least one committed artifact. A result nobody can open is a summary, not evidence.

migrated-record-that-never-says-where-it.reason: Every migrated record states where its input came from, including when the answer is that nothing was issued. Leaving it out is how a synthetic workload passes for a captured one.

migrated-record-with-no-repeatable-ident.reason: A migrated record carries either its immutable identifiers or the record that names them. Without one it cannot be repeated, whatever its level.

migrated-record-without-limitations.reason: A migrated record states its limitations. A record with none is a result nobody bounded.

record-still-carrying-a-certification-le.reason: certificationLevel is not a v1alpha2 field. A legacy value belongs under legacyClassification, where it is marked as carried rather than current.

certified-claim-with-no-record.reason: A certified claim rests on at least one record. Certified and citing nothing is the failure the register exists to refuse.

claim-carrying-a-certification-level.reason: certificationLevel is not a v1alpha2 field at any depth. The legacy value has one place: legacyClassification.

claim-carrying-an-evidence-level.reason: A level belongs to a record. A claim carrying one is the v1alpha1 shape under a new field name, and it cannot express three records at three levels.

not-claimed-claim-without-a-reason.reason: not-claimed states why. A blank reason turns the status into somewhere to put a claim nobody wants to discuss.

planned-claim-citing-a-record.reason: A claim nothing has proven cites no record. One that points at a record reads as proven.
